en: The Vow of the Great Master Zhiyi of Tiantai:
Now, those who wish to recite [the scriptures] in order to extinguish karmic obstacles and assist toward Bodhi must first make a vow.
Having first purified the three karmas, joining the ten fingers in palms-together salutation and facing the Buddhas, they should speak these words as follows:

The disciple, Bhikṣu [Name] (the other assemblies each recite their names accordingly), bows his head in prostration and pays homage with single-minded devotion to all Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time,
the Honored Dharma, Prajñā, and the twelve divisions of the True, Pure, and Wondrous Dharma. All...

To the great assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, the various worthy and holy Saṅghas, and the eternally abiding Triple Gem: I pray that by your divine power, you will look upon us with compassion and mindfulness.

May you bear witness to this. By the roots of goodness and merit of this recitation, may they be dedicated exclusively to adorning the four debts of gratitude and all sentient beings throughout the ten directions and the entire Dharma-realm. May I, together with all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, [attain liberation].

From time immemorial until this day, due to ignorance and delusion, the six sense organs and three karmic actions have created all manner of offenses that obstruct the Path, whether coarse or subtle, as known by the Buddha; may they all be extinguished at once, throughout all future lives.

May they forever leave behind the bodies of hell-beings, hungry ghosts, and animals; may they forever leave behind the female body; may they forever leave behind the bodies of those in borderlands, the low-born, and those subject to the eight difficulties.

May they, together with all sentient beings of the Dharma-realm, whether in this life or in future lives, always encounter spiritual friends and always hear the unsurpassed True Dharma of the Mahāyāna, thereby attaining realization of the eternally abiding [nature] within this very body.

The Buddha-nature, the ocean of Great Nirvana, and all dharmas are fundamentally quiescent and extinguished from the beginning. Possessing great Bodhi, one thoroughly understands the faculties and their objects, as well as the subject and object of cognition.

In a single thought-moment, when the mind arises, all dharmas are complete: the hundred realms and three thousand worlds, emptiness, provisionality, and the Middle Way—this is the Seal of the Dharma-realm, inconceivable.
Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings are non-dual in their threefold lack of distinction. Realizing the provisional and awakening to the real, one brings forth...
The Great Bodhicitta seeks enlightenment above and transforms beings below; it uproots the suffering of birth and death and bestows ultimate bliss.

One cultivates firm and powerful diligence and the four kinds of samādhi—namely, the inconceivable single contemplation and triple contemplation—and contemplates the inconceivable single truth and triple truths.

When the contemplation of the truths merges into oneness, the four māras and three hindrances are transcended. Through all conditions and encountered objects, one perfects the circle by means of the wondrous ten dharmas.

Riding upon this vehicle, practice and understanding further support one another; mind after mind becomes luminous and tranquil. One awakens to the true Middle Way and opens the Buddha’s knowledge and vision. Mind after mind manifests before one;
the entire body of wisdom does not arise from the awakening of another, but flows spontaneously into the ocean of *sarvajñā* (all-knowledge).

Abiding in the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), one possesses great wisdom and accomplishes the Mahāyāna. One penetrates all gradual and sudden teachings, and by breaking open a single mote of dust, one emerges.

The sūtras of the great trichiliocosm and the Buddha-dharmas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are all understood within a single thought-moment. Awakened to the compassion of the Buddhas, he is free from all stinginess and parsimony.
He expounds upon *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā*, bestowing them universally upon all. Opening the gate and emptying the treasury, he gives away the wish-fulfilling jewel (*cintāmaṇi*).

Through the stages of principle, name, contemplative practice, semblance, partial realization, and ultimate perfection—the three points of the perfect *ī*—they are neither vertical nor horizontal. This is the Great City of the True Dharma.
The Vajra Treasure Storehouse: all Buddha-dharmas, through which one accomplishes both self-cultivation and the transformation of others within a single lifetime.
Even if one has not yet attained full clarity, this is the cause of causes; from cause one elicits fruit, and from non-fruit one attains the supreme fruition.
May I, together with all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, at the time of death—seven days prior—spontaneously know the moment of transition and have no inverted thoughts.
The mind is undisturbed; the mind is not associated with discursive thoughts. Body and mind are free from all suffering and pain.
Sitting cross-legged in right mindfulness, body and mind are peaceful and blissful. Entering into profound samādhi, one beholds the Buddhas of the ten directions.

May the World-Honored Amitābha, the Buddhas of the three periods of time, Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, all the great Bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly of holy ones, not forsake their original vows and appear before me in person, together.

At that time, a great radiance was emitted, illuminating and touching their bodies and minds. All their karmic hindrances were instantly extinguished. Their faculties became suddenly clear, and they entered deeply into knowledge and vision.
By means of great supernatural power, [the Buddha] sustained their bodies and minds, extended his golden hand to stroke their heads and guide them.
Rejoicing and leaping for joy, they rode upon the power of the Buddha’s vows and sat upon vajra pedestals, following after the Tathāgata and the assembly of holy ones. At that—
In a single thought-moment, they are born by transformation upon a golden lotus in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss of Amitābha Buddha.

They awaken to and enter the various patiences of non-arising and tranquil extinction, transcending to the higher stages. They obtain the six supernormal powers and abide in the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, remaining unmoved within the nature of reality (dharmatā).
In a single thought-moment, they travel throughout the ten directions to serve all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Before each and every Buddha, there was my own body, performing all manner of offerings, hearing the Dharma, and receiving predictions of enlightenment.

At once, I was able to universally receive and uphold the profound ocean of the Dharma of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time; I attained clear understanding by myself, without awakening through another.
Great Principle, Great Vow, Great Adornment, Great Wisdom and Severance, Great Universal Knowledge, Great Path, Great Function, Great Expedient Means and Reality, Great...
Benefit. Great non-abiding. All the *pāramitā* practices of all Buddhas are cultivated simultaneously.
One becomes a companion to great beings such as Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra. One fulfills all the immeasurable and boundless vast practices and vows of all Bodhisattvas.
One attains all the great *dhāraṇī* gates and all the *samādhi* gates, and universally knows all...

In an instant, throughout all the paths of atoms in the ten directions within the pure adornments of the Buddha-fields, he attained equal and perfect enlightenment, turned the great wheel of Dharma, and liberated sentient beings; his unconditioned compassion universally covered the entire dharma-realm.

Without moving from the true limit (*bhūtakoṭi*), they universally enter the three periods of time to deliver all sentient beings. Sometimes they manifest in the body of a Buddha to bestow both the provisional and the real;
sometimes they take the form of the nine realms to proclaim the gradual and the sudden, requesting the turning of the gradual and sudden teachings and propagating the gradual and sudden teachings.

Through the three wheels of conversion, their gathering and transforming of beings is inexhaustible, equaling the pervasiveness of empty space as they perform Buddha-work. From their primordial source, they descend to manifest traces, gathering and transforming beings.

The trace returns to the source; though the trace and the source differ, they are one in inconceivable reality. When the practices for self and others are perfected, the secret treasury of eternal abiding is revealed.
May all beings within the Dharma-realm, whether enemies or kin, together enter this ocean of vows.
